entities.summary:
José Presas y Marull was a Spanish attorney, writer, politician, diplomat, and historian of Catalan origin who served as the private secretary of Carlota Joaquina of Spain.

Born in 1780 in Sant Feliu de Guíxols, Catalonia, Spain, Presas y Marull came from a prominent Catalan family and was educated at the University of Barcelona.

He was a prominent figure in Catalan politics and served as a member of the Cortes Generales, the Spanish parliament, from 1812 to 1814.

In 1825, he was appointed as the private secretary of Carlota Joaquina, the granddaughter of King Ferdinand VII of Spain, and played a key role in her attempts to maintain her claim to the Spanish throne.

Presas y Marull was a prolific writer and published several books on Catalan history and culture, including 'La historia de los preses de Sant Feliu de Guíxols' (The History of the Preses of Sant Feliu de Guíxols).

He died in 1842 at the age of 62.

In his legacy, Presas y Marull is remembered as a champion of Catalan culture and identity, and his writings continue to be studied by scholars today.

His most striking statistic is that he was one of the first Catalan politicians to use the Catalan language in official contexts, paving the way for future generations of Catalan nationalists.

As he once said, 'La cultura catalana és la cultura de l'home' (Catalan culture is the culture of man).

Presas y Marull's story is a testament to the enduring power of culture and identity in shaping the course of human history.
